Payloads: Decent stay but could have been better We were in NYC for the US Open for labor day weekend. The location was a contributing factor for this decision as well. It was a bit tight especially when the pull out bed was open. Closet space is very limited. Safe in closet fits laptop. Free internet access in rooms not wi-fi though. We paid $330 per night and includes breakfast. Valet parking or nightly parking is $48 per night. If you take your car out during the day and check it back in, that's an extra $48. We were disappointed coz we asked for early check-in yet when we got there around 1 pm, the room was not ready. They said they would call when the room was ready but didn't. So we came back at 3:40 pm and they gave us the keys. Also we requested an extra hour for late check out - 12 noon instead of 11 am but they flat out refused. Payloads: much maligned, great place for family vacation after reading some of the reviews preceding our stay i was pretty concerned that i hadn't made the best selection, but i was pleasantly surprised by our experience at this resort. it's beautifully landscaped, the service was friendly and helpful. we requested an updated suite upon early check-in and were given a squeaky clean, well-situated suite. plenty of room and privacy for two adults and two 14-year-olds. it's a perfect resort for those with children or teens because there are so many pools and activities, especially the golf. i was worried that we should have gone to the pointe hilton tapatio cliffs, but after a visit there for lunch we all agreed that squaw peak was superior for our needs.the food is a bit pricey, but that's typical of a resort. we made our way down the block three times to aunt chilada's for lunch and dinner which is a fun, affordable and delicious alternative to the restaurants onsite. the concierge staff was extremely helpful in giving us restaurant recommendations and maps.i would definitely stay here again!

Payloads: great time, excellent amenities slight problem with the reservation. when we called in march the week before we were to arrive, they told us that our reservation change (made in december) was not listed anywhere in their files. the reservations agent was pleasant, but said he couldnt change the reservation and we would have to check out a day earlier than planned. since this was a reward trip, we were upset but just had him book a room for one night in sedona (since we were going there anyway)my wife checked in on monday afternoon with the kids. she asked for and got an upgrade to a casita. she asked when we were checking out, and they had the change in place (magic?). she didn't say a word, just cancelled the sedona reservation. i arrived in the evening and was very impressed with the casita. the ground floor had a full kitchen and dinning room, half bath plus a living room with fold out bed and tv. you walk upstairs to a bedroom and full bath, with a private balcony off of the bedroom.while we did have a car, i dont understand why previous posters said there was nothing within walking distance other than aunt chilada's. there was a strip shopping center just across the street with a chinese carryout and some sort of sports bar. 1/2 mile away was a drug strore/liquor store and across the street from that was a supermarket.the kids enjoyed the lazy river, tubes and minature golf. we ended up buying the resort package, although the golf would have been free since we were diamond level, but i was sending and receiving large faxes and it made doing this more economical. both restaurants were open. no complaints about the food. i read these posts and always wonder about the resorts - some people are very negative, some are very positive. i have found a balanced report is more telling. just my $ 0.02

Payloads: good deal my husband and i stayed for 3 nights in february. we had reserved a standard room, but had to upgrade to a club room. the standard was dark, cramped, smelled stale and had very worn/unattractive bedding. nothing like the cheerful picture the hotel features online. the club room was nicely furnished, modern and had a large bathroom. it looked exactly like the photo on their website. my only complaint was the tolitries were never replenished. the complimentary breakfast was basic, but plentiful - yogurt, granola, pastry, juice, coffee. overall, it was a fantastic deal for the location. we would definitely stay here again, unbeatable value and perfect location.

Payloads: very pretty hotel with nice service but average room i just returned from a weekend trip for business at the royal palms. i was put in regular room next to the road. the room had low ceilings, a small bathroom and no water pressure. the room was very dark because the main window looked out to the walkway to the other rooms so if you opened your blinds anybody in the hallway could look right in your room. truely an awful setup. i also requested a king bed but was given two doubles instead. the beds were extremely comfortable but i don't like to travel and stay in a bed smaller than mine at home. i was told they would move me the next day but never contacted me so i didn't bother to switch. the tv was an old zenith 25 inch with a dull picture. also the towels were very small for a five star hotel. the pool was small and the lounge chairs all occupied. you had to wait for the pool guy to find you a chair once somebody left. it was a very quite and adult type area and not very good for children. on the positive side, the staff was very friendly and went out of their way to be helpful and caring. the food at all the functions was great and the grounds are wonderful. the lobby is warm and inviting. overall a lovely resort but the room was just so dark and depressing i'm not sure i would want to stay there again unless i could get a room in another location. i've stayed at most of the other upscale places in scottsdale and the darkness of the room was a real turnoff. i also missed not having a golf course on the grounds. i would not bring my kids to this resort as it would be a real dissapointment for them compared to the phoenician, biltmore, hyatt, or princess.

elevator area carpet during our stay there) but for $180 per night including breakfast for four it was a good deal for la.

Payloads: good budget hotel having stayed at alot of budget hotels, i can honestly tell you about the good, the bad, and the ugly. adante hotel definitely falls into the good catagory. once again, this is a budget hotel.....so if you're looking for luxury, this is not for you. but if you're going to be out sightseeing all day (like me) and stop by the room every now and then, and want a good place to crash at nite, then this is the place for you. i was pleasantly surprised when i arrived at the hotel. check-in was a breeze. the front desk clerk was friendly and very helpful. the room itself was spotless, although somewhat small....ok for 1 or 2 people, but that's it. i liked the funky paintjob. the bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was exceptionally clean...looked brand new. the room also included a large closet with ironing board and iron. internet acess was provided as well as coffee pot with selection of coffee/teas. bottled water was provided at extra charge and was clearly labled as such. cable tv also provided. no ac, but there was a large ceiling fan that did the job. continental breakfast was included from 7-9am at no extra charge. there is an elevator, but it is somewhat slow. my only complaints....bathroom towels were kinda cheap, maid service will knock on your door at 8am...loudly... if you don't hang the do not disturb sign on the door, and the view from my room was that of a brick wall. so except for these few minor things, i would definitely stay at the adante again. a couple of extra notes....adante hotel is in the union square area, not on union square. in fact, it's quite a bit of an uphill walk from union square and the bart/muni public transport stations. this can be kinda annoying if you've been walking around the city all day. there is a bus stop right in front of the hotel, so you may want to take that instead of walking. the cool thing is that the powell street cable car line is very close. and yes, the neighborhood has it's share of crack [--] and street people. but if you're used to large city life, you won't care. when i was there, these people mainly kept to themselves. i'ts not nearly as bad as you might think by reading some other people's reviews. so, all in all, adante hotel is a good place to stay for the budget sightseer or student traveller. i would go back again.

Payloads: lovely boutique hotel in convenient location having stayed at the argonaut on a previous trip, we were interested to see how the tuscan would compare. it did not disappoint and cost less for our 4 day stay. the location is fantastic - a 5 minute walk to the wharf and close to bus and trolley stops.having read previous reviews, we requested a courtyard room. we were given a room on the 4th floor with a view of a partially constructed building. we were not not concerned about the lack of view as we did not intend spending much time in our room but we did wonder whether there would be any early morning noise. our concerns were unfounded as we did not hear a sound.the room was a nice size and beautifully furnished. the bed was comfortable and the bathroom was clean with a nice selection of toiletries. there was a fully-stocked fridge with snacks and drinks. although we didn't use it, there was free internet access in the room. we did however make use of the pc/internet access available in the lobby without cost.the staff at the front desk could not have been more helpful and whilst we did not avail his services, the concierge always seemed to be busy with guests giving info and advice.the wine reception is a good way to wind down at the end of a busy day sightseeing and also to meet and share experiences with other guests. there was also a gentleman offering massage at this time and we met a few people who had enjoyed his services.upon checking-in, we were told that we would receive complementary continental breakfast for each morning of our stay. we do not usually rate these well but this was really nice - a large dish of fresh fruit, croissant or a muffin, juice and coffee. we also ate dinner at the hotel restaurant (cafe pescatore) one night. the food and service were both excellent.the only negative point was that when we booked our airport transfer through the hotel, we were charged $10 more than the going rate.all in all, we would recommend a stay at the tuscan and would definitely stay there again.

Payloads: return visit--gets better each time i am a bit late in writing this review. it seems life hasn't slowed down long enough since our return to get it done.i have appreciated all the reviews i have read, and whether good or bad have learned something from everyones opinions. here are my opinions of the resort, as well as my experiences.we were a group of nine that travelled in mid to late feb. there were 4 adults, and 5 kids ranging in age from 9 to 17. for my husband, myself and our 3 kids aged 9-14 this was our second trip to this resort in just under a year. we were there at easter in 2007. we loved it so much the first time that we jumped at an opportunity to go back with my brother and his wife and 2 kids. airport-- although the airport itself has nothing to do with the resort, the transfers do, so i thought i would give you a few quick observations. our luggage was the last to come off the carousel, (thats what you get for being first at the airport in your departure city i guess) so by the time we got all our bags the airport was pretty empty. we opted to carry our bags out to our tourbus ourselves since we had them so nicely stacked on the carts. we were not bombarded by the guys asking to take our bags because we were so far behind everyone, so we just said no thank-you to the 1 or 2 guys that did try to help. that was a big mistake. we were unaware that you are not alowed to take the luggage carts out to the parking lot, so at the last second, as our bus was getting ready to take off, we were scrambling to carry our numerous bags out to the lot. a piece of advice--if you have more bags than you can comfortably handle, just let the guys take them for you and pay them a few bucks. it simplifies things so much. when we fianally got to the bus with our bags, it was like a feeding frenzy of people grabbing our bags and throwing them under into the storage compartment that we lost sight of our carry-ons, which then got thrown up onto a different truck to be transported to the resort because the storage compartment on the bus was full. we were scared we would never see them again, and the hotel rep on the bus warned us that we should never let our small bags like carry-ons be stored like that because they can go missing too easily. it was not our intention to ever let them out of our hands, but in the confusion stuff happens. i am happy to say though that all items made it safe and sound to our rooms.trip to resort-- check in-- the ride went smoothly. it seemed like a much smoother ride than lastyear. our check-in was done there on the bus. be sure you have your passports, and confirmation letter with you on the ride, as you will need these things for the check-in procedure. a pen is helpful too. when we were given our package we were informed that we had been upgraded to diamond becuase we were returning guests. we were given diamond bracelets, but my brother and his family were given the golden bracelets. it didn't really make any difference as far as we could tell, because we were still in the golden villas, which is where we preferred to be. at this point we noticed that, although we were all put in the same villa, our rooms were not on the same floor. i had written the resort earlier and requested connecting rooms because of the kids. i understand it is not guaranteed, and is nothing more than a request. lastyear we got exactly what we asked for, this year we did not get connecting rooms, and furthermore the rooms were not even on the same floor. a bit of a problem since i had only packed one of everything (like toothpaste, shampoo, contact solution etc) and because, quite frankly i was looking forward to spending some time with my husband on this trip........ once we got to the resort, the moms headed straight to the golden reception to tried to work out the room situation and the dads and kids went to the rooms. the golden rep was extremely helpful. he wasn't able to get us the connecting rooms, but juggled around some people that had not yet arrived and managed to get us in rooms beside each other. it still wasn't ideal, but my husband stayed in one room with the boys, and my daughter and i stayed in the other room. it actually turned out ok, cuz i didn't have to listen to the old guy snore all night after having too much to drink...hahah. the golden rep also gave us our safe rental for free because we were returning guests. a nice perk again. at this time i tried to book our a'la cartes, but they only do bookings until 8 at night, and it was after this time. then he informed me that they had made reservations for us already, and if they were not suitable then we coud come back in the morning and change them. i found this to be a nice added touch, Payloads: great hotel! i stayed at this hotel for two nights while on business in hollywood, ca and i really enjoyed my stay. this is a great hotel (high 4 stars) and it is very different from most luxury hotels i've stayed at. the design is modern and chique and this fits in well with hollywood blvd. overall, i enjoyed the atmosphere, the cleanliness of the hotel, the quality of the accommodations, and the convenience to where i needed to be. also, it was nice meeting celebrities by the pool at night!here are some things i did not like:1. no heat. there was ac only. at night, temperatures in la dropped to 30 degrees and heat was needed.2. there is only a fitted sheet and a comforter on the bed. there is no sheets between the fitted sheet and the comforter. you use the comforter as your only blanket. while the front desk assured me they clean each comforter every night, i like a sheet and i found this unusual.3. the bathroom was dimly lit.4. the lobby is a historic and well decorated lobby. yet, it has the atmosphere of a night club. there is virtually no light except for candles and i thought this was a shame. it's an impressive lobby and i would have liked to enjoy this room.

Payloads: the biltmore is horrendous i am just finishing up a two-week stay at the millenium biltmore. i had to travel to l.a. for business and needed a hotel downtown. i was told that the biltmore was a nice place with good services. unfortunately, that could not be farther from the truth. although the common areas of the hotel are beautiful, the roooms are badly outdated. the bed is extremely uncomfortable and the bathroom is tiny and grimy. the hotel gym is nothing more than a hallway with some old free weights and equally old cardio machines. the most disturbing thing about the hotel, however, is the utter lack of professionalism of its staff. other than the concierge, the staff is unfriendly, not knowledgeable and generally unhelpful. the laundry service is ridiculously expensive which is not unusual, but it is untimely, often taking a day longer than promised, which is totally unacceptable when you are trying to do business. i recommend that anyone considering this hotel reconsider immediately. you will absolutely be disappointed in your choice. the hilton checkers is across the street and is a much nicer and professional establishment. i will never stay at the millenium again.

Payloads: going on a cruise? - great place to stay my husband and i stayed here in large part based on the reviews we found here. we stayed for 2 nights before our cruise.check-in was hassle free. the room was smaller, but really - it was nice. granite countertops and nice shower head in the bathrooms. huge closet (all those cruise bags, right?).bayside was right across the street - there were numerous restaurants - including hooters, bubba gump, chilis. there were also traveler shops, food court, standard shopping, etc. near the hotel is also a walgreens for any last minute things you need.taxis are out front waiting to take you to the cruise port. i would definately stay here again.

Payloads: somehwat disappointed although the resort was lush and green and looked inviting from the outside, i was a bit disappointed in the suite itself.as i work in the hotel and hospitality industry in las vegas, i took notice to certain things regarding the room itself. i was disappointed when i did not see a luggage rack. the waste basket in the powder room had a very narrow opening and in my opinion, wasn't very effective.we stayed in the north building adjacent to the pool area and a couple of the restarants and shopping. however, i felt like the map of the campus was really not to scale since we had to drive all over looking for the spa and salon the following morning and hoping we weren't late to out appointment. the building for the spa and salon was not signed very well and with the construction going on it was difficult to manuever around the campus.the spa and salon was a treat and the staff was very welcoming and made both myself and my sister feel well taken care of and pampered. the cranberry/apple ice tea they offered us was delicious.since i prepaid through hotels.com and just posted a credit card for incidentals, check out was a breeze however i was disappointed that i wasn't asked how the room was, how are stay was or anything. i also had to report that on the morning of check out, we found ants in the room. the agent made note but didn't seem too concerned nor did she offer apologies.i also didn't notice until i returned home to las vegas that evening that i had 4 bites on my foot and ankle. mosquito, ant or bed bug i don't know but after a week they are still not gone.my overall opinion of the resort is fair and i would score it a 3 but i don't know that i would return.

Payloads: you people are so wrong if you think the roosevelt's sucks! my goodness. it really surprises me that people feel that a 3 star hotel should be double its rating and also remain the price they paid. the roosevelt is a wonderful place. clean, yes clean, and extremely helpful staff. anytime that i had to speak to the reception, they were very courteous. this was our first experience of valet parking - also very friendly people. the gift shop, although opening/closing at any time, was stocked with what we needed so as not to dip into the minbar so often and the man in charge there was always happy to chat. extremely comfortable beds (we had a tower room) and a more-than adequate bathroom (i have been in 5 stars where the bathroom is smaller). as for the neighborhood - yes it is a bit sleazy but it is hollywood!!!! Payloads: perfect location!! while it's true that it is not the perfect place, believe me when i say that it is actually a diamond in the rough. my boyfriend and i came to visit seattle for the first time this year, we stayed for 4 days/3nights and since i knew we were going to be out of the hotel the majority of our days with sightseeing i decided to book a room here. best decision i ever made!!my pros:- everything is within walking distance (space needle is practically in your backyard, belltown with all the restaurants, bars, and clubs is just a few blocks down the street and the pike place market is about a 10 minute walk away or you can hop on a bus to go deeper downtown, etc)- rooms are clean.- heater worked really well- they have room service, and their staff of servers are pretty considerate and nice- free wireless internet service and it's fast!- room service called us to ask if we needed new towels or anything else.- my boyfriend bought fish at pike's market, which was delivered to this hotel. they were nice enough to store it in their restaurant freezer for us free of charge!some cons:- you have to pay for parking- the hallways kind of scared me upon getting off the elevator because it seemed pretty dingy (they need to do some steam cleaning or something - i would not want to walk around on bare feet!)- the construction zone next to the hotel might worry people but seriously, we didn't hear any of that noise through the walls or anything in the morning.- the people at the front desk can be a little nicer but that really wasn't a big deal to us.overall, we enjoyed our stay at this hotel because of its location. you can pretty much see almost everything there is to see in seattle (or at least the best places if not everything) if you stay here and you wouldn't even need a car!

Payloads: glad we stayed! five ladies from wisconsin stayed at the hospitality house from may 24 thru the 29th. five nights. we had no trouble finding it, the entrance is small and not fancy. we had a two bedroom/one bath, full kitchen, living, dining room combined. it was more than enough room. one bedroom had a king bed, the second a queen and the living room area had a full pull out bed in the sofa. each bedroom had a tv as well as the main room. a few times we could have used another bathroom but we just took turns and finished with makeup, hair etc in the bedrooms. it was nice having the fruit, cereal, muffins, juice and milk every morning. the front desk was helpful. we were mostly there in the late evening as we did alot of the touristy things all day long. we could easily have had another adult with us.the cost per night was $380.36, this included all fees and taxes. we each paid for one night. we all thought where it was located was great. we would hightly recommend it for a larger group wanting to stay together. its in a nice area, restaurants right next door and shopping just up the street.

Payloads: Wonderful Service...Beautiful Location! My husband and I stayed at the Majestic from Dec 21 to 28, 2006. We were there to attend my cousin's wedding, which made this a unique experience. Below, a brief overview of our fantastic trip:FOOD: If your idea of a dream vacation is gourmet food and spectacular dining experiences, I would recommend against all-inclusives in general. All-inclusives tend to have a formula: breakfast, lunch and dinner buffets, a few specialty restaurants, and more casual eats near the beach. You will not go hungry, but you will rarely have a magical experience. Le Gourmet had a couple of very nice dishes (squash soup, veal), and the Rodeo Steak House surprised us with an amazing steak and fries. At Matsuri, we asked them to make a custom sushi roll (rolled in tempura batter and fried) which was fantastic!! Overall, the buffets were varied enough for a week's stay and fairly tasty. I was trying to be careful not to get sick, so I stuck to simple stuff and I was fine.ROOMS: I thought the room was beautiful! I agree with the reviews regarding the bathrooms being not private enough. I was there with my husband so it wasn't a problem, but if you are sharing a room with kids it could be tricky. Take advantage of the jacuzzi tub!! Beds were comfortable, air conditioning was perfect.POOL: I LOVED the pool. It was crystal clear and we didn't have a problem getting pool chairs up to about 1pm. The swim-up bar was great! Tip the bartender your first few times, ask him his name and get to know him, and pretty soon he'll be pouring you very generous drinks. Bring an insulated mug; you'll have to go back for refills less often and you'll keep the bugs out!BEACH: Beautiful beach! I love the fine white sand. The beach chairs get full pretty early. Personally I prefer the pool since I don't like a bikini full of sand at the end of the day, but the ocean water was warm. Waves can be a bit rough - keep an eye on non-swimmers.SNORKELING: We would not recommend going snorkeling with the company that operates at the Majestic beach. They would not give us a group rate for 12 people, their boat was 40 minutes late, and the boat captain was impatient and barely spoke English. They said they would take us to a site that was calm and good for beginners and that they would have a ladder for people to get back in the boat. Instead, we went to a choppy site, four people on our boat threw up, there was no ladder and people injured themselves being hauled back into the boat, and to top it off, the coral was all dead at the site they took us to. NOT WORTH THE MONEY.SERVICE: I was impressed with the service. Anytime we asked for anything (more towels, water, specially made meals, various wedding-related requests) they were more than happy to accomo

Payloads: great location, clean rooms, we enjoyed our visit.... we stayed at this hotel the first week of august. we really enjoyed our stay here. the location is great. it is a short walk to fisherman's wharf, the f line, pier 39 etc but is far enough away away from the ticky tacky areas. the hotel was clean and decorated nicely. the rooms are a bit small, but not uncomfortably so. the linens and bed were comfortable. the shower head was stong and the water was nice and warm.on the first part of our stay, we were in a courtyard room. this made the room seem a bit larger by the way that it was set up. when we returned later in the week we were put in an outside room. it was noisier and even with the shutters closed the light from the safeway sign kept the room pretty bright. i work night shift and am used to sleeping during the daylight, but for people who like it dark, that might be more difficult. the second room also smelled a bit musty (think mothballs) and we could never get it aired out. only a mild inconvenience though.the am coffee/tea/biscotti is nice. it was a nice stop before heading out for a bigger breakfast. only participated in the evening reception once. the wine was good, but the appetizers were gone. lots of people take advantage of this time, it was always busy.we did eat at the hotel restaurant for one breakfast. the food was ok...and the service was just ok too. nothing to write home about for the price. next time i would probably go somewhere else.the front desk staff recommended fior d'italia for a dinner reservation. it was a 2 block walk and so great!! it was a wonderful suggestion. we also enjoyed the stinking rose on another afternoon.the tuscan inn is a great hotel and we would return again.

Payloads: Nie trip to Majestic Colonial We just returned from a 7night stay (5/23-5/30/07) at the Majestic Colonial. Let me preface this review by stating that this was our 4th AI vacation, and give our vacation background: We honeymooned in August 2003 at Sandals Antigua, and have vacationed the past 2 springs in Cancun at the Iberostar Paraiso Maya (2005) and Secrets Exellence Riviera Cancun (2006). All of these properties have been rated as 5 or 5+ stars on all travel websites that I have visited. Given our vacation history, I cannot rank the Majestic as a 5star resort. It was a nice resort, and there was nothing missing, but after visiting superior properties, the differences were glaringly obvious. That said, we still had a wonderful time, and have no major complaints at all about or vacation.Check-in: Upon arrival, we were immediately greeted with the aforementioned cold towel and a Majestic. We arrived at a time when there were very few other people checking in or out, so were processed through very quickly. The front desk staff were very friendly. However, our room requests were not granted. We booked a Colonial Jr Suite, and I requested building 2 or 3, closer to the beach than the lobby. Therefore, I was very disappointed to discover we had been assigned room 1407. This room was in building 1, and was the Col Jr Suite closest to the lobby. I was even more disappointed upon arrival at our room to discover that both our balcony and terrace overlooked the neighboring property's parking lot. I have to admit that after all the research I did, and knowing which buildings I preferred to be in, that this room location was terribly disappointing, and probably to some extent tainted my view of our entire vacation (just being honest here).Room: Our room was very nice. We had a Colonial Jr Suite, which was on the top floor of our building. There were only 2 Col Jr Suites per block of rooms (and not all blocks had them). It was pretty much exactly as all the pics I saw. As our room was top floor, we had a vaulted ceiling (which was nice). The bathroom was as desribed, but the glass on the doors to the shower and toilet were longer than I expected and the frosting was completely non-see-through, so no problems there. The bed was very hard, and very uncomfortable. And the pillows a bit odd--1 wasn't thick enough, but 2 gave a bad crick in the neck. In addition to the regular balcony that all rooms had on the back of the room, we also had a private terrace with a jacuzzi tub on the side of the room. This was wonderful, and I am very glad that I upgraded for it. We used the terrace just about every day. I layed out topless a few times, as no one could see into our terrace. We also used the jacuzzi as a private pool, and filled it with cold water during the day if we were laying out on the terrace. Only used it as a hot tub one time in the evening, but still got good use out of it.Food/Dining: We did not have any stomach prblems at all (in contrast to our last 2 trips to Mexio). In fact, the breakfast and lunch buffets at the Supreme Buffet were some of the best that I have had at any AI! There were some hot food stations that stayed the same everyday (eggs, omlettes, crepes and waffles made to order for breakfast; pasta made to order and grilled meats at lunch), but the pre-prepared hot foods were different every day. My usual breakfast consisted of fruit and yogurt, 2 churros, and 1-2 crepes. The freshly grilled chicken and the rice option at lunch were always very good. On one of our last days there, I discovered that the chef could make pesto pasta, and it was great (especially when adding a scoop of the cream sauce). The deserts were surprisingly good on the buffet (which has not been the case at other AI's we have visited). Even hubby agreed that the chocolate cakes were some of the best we have had.Dinner was hit or miss. . . . Day 1: Matsuri. This was OK. I had lemon chicken (which was decent), hubby ordered seafood chow-mein, but got beef instead. Appetizers, sushi and deserts were fair.Day 2: Rodeo Steakhouse. We both got the Chateaubriand, which we both thought was the best meal we had while there. The steak was really, really good, while the side dishes left a bit to be desired. We had really great service here, especially from the wine/water guy, so gave him a tip as well.Day 3: Taino. We had really bad service here. No waiter for at least 10 minutes, and we got our food before anyone offered us a drink. This was also an odd set-up. They had a Dominican buffet set up as an appetizer bar, and you ordered off a menu that was Mexican, but it was Mexican unlike any other I have experienced. I actually thought the Dominican buffet was quite good, and should have just eaten that for my dinner--what I got wasn't very good at all. I would recommend that you try the buffet first and see if you can get enough to eat before ordering off the menu. The local foods were quite interesting, and surprisingly tasty.Day 4: Supreme Buffet. We were tired this day, and didn't feel like dressing up, so just went to the buffet. It was pretty much the same as lunch, plus a few additional appetizers and deserts. Still good, just nothing spectacular.Day 5: We were supposed to go to the gourmet, but our reservation got mixed up, so we went back to the steakhouse and got the Chateaubriand again. Just as good the second time.Day 6: Teppanyaki Grill. Great service, great show, great food. Sure, I know that I can get the same thing at home, so it wasn't anything special, but we both agreed that this was our second best meal at the Majestic. There was a nice appitizer platter, and you got TONS of food! The shrimp was a bit overcooked, but I was pleasantly surprised by the fish and beef. Day 7: Gourmet. Surprisingly, after our reservation snafu on sunday, we were able to get a reservation for our last night there without a problem. This meal took a while to serve (we were there for close to an hour and a half). The appetizers were a bit strange, but the pumpkin soup was fabulous. The puff pastry crust really makes it! We both had surf and turf (beef wellington with a little bit of lobster in the center of the roll). It was OK. Deserts were pretty good. Hubby had tiramisu, and I had the Majestic Pinapple which was kind of like a thick flavored creme brulee.Pool: HUGE!!! There was a place for everyone at the pool! Lots of chairs, so never had a problem getting a lounger. They have these little ledges all around the pool where you can lay, or move your chair so that your feet can dip into the water. These are very nice! The animation team was centered at the swim-up bar, so it was very noisy there, and something was always going on. Lots of drunk people planing games. LOL. After a day or two, we gravitated towards the quiet end of the pool. There was a bar there, too, although not swim-up. There were no servers delivering drinks to patrons at any of the pool bars, they were all self-service. The spa pool was also connected to (but separated by a partial wall from ) the main pool, and the water there was about 10-15 degrees cooler. Let me preface this review by stating that this was our 4th AI vacation, and give our vacation background: We honeymooned in August 2003 at Sandals Antigua, and have vacationed the past 2 springs in Cancun at the Iberostar Paraiso Maya (2005) and Secrets Exellence Riviera Cancun (2006). All of these properties have been rated as 5 or 5  stars on all travel websites that I have visited. Given our vacation history, I cannot rank the Majestic as a 5star resort. It was a nice resort, and there was nothing missing, but after visiting superior properties, the differences were glaringly obvious. That said, we still had a wonderful time, and have no major complaints at all about or vacation.Check-in: Upon arrival, we were immediately greeted with the aforementioned cold towel and a Majestic. We arrived at a time when there were very few other people checking in or out, so were processed through very quickly. The front desk staff were very friendly. However, our room requests were not granted. We booked a Colonial Jr Suite, and I requested building 2 or 3, closer to the beach than the lobby. Therefore, I was very disappointed to discover we had been assigned room 1407. This room was in building 1, and was the Col Jr Suite closest to the lobby. I was even more disappointed upon arrival at our room to discover that both our balcony and terrace overlooked the neighboring property's parking lot. I have to admit that after all the research I did, and knowing which buildings I preferred to be in, that this room location was terribly disappointing, and probably to some extent tainted my view of our entire vacation (just being honest here).Room: Our room was very nice. We had a Colonial Jr Suite, which was on the top floor of our building. There were only 2 Col Jr Suites per block of rooms (and not all blocks had them). It was pretty much exactly as all the pics I saw. As our room was top floor, we had a vaulted ceiling (which was nice). The bathroom was as desribed, but the glass on the doors to the shower and toilet were longer than I expected and the frosting was completely non-see-through, so no problems there. The bed was very hard, and very uncomfortable. And the pillows a bit odd--1 wasn't thick enough, but 2 gave a bad crick in the neck. In addition to the regular balcony that all rooms had on the back of the room, we also had a private terrace with a jacuzzi tub on the side of the room. This was wonderful, and I am very glad that I upgraded for it. We used the terrace just about every day. I layed out topless a few times, as no one could see into our terrace. We also used the jacuzzi as a private pool, and filled it with cold water during the day if we were laying out on the terrace. Only used it as a hot tub one time in the evening, but still got good use out of it.Food/Dining: We did not have any stomach prblems at all (in contrast to our last 2 trips to Mexio). There were some hot food stations that stayed the same everyday (eggs, omlettes, crepes and waffles made to order for breakfast; pasta made to order and grilled meats at lunch), but the pre-prepared hot foods were different every day. On one of our last days there, I discovered that the chef could make pesto pasta, and it was great (especially when adding a scoop of the cream sauce). We both got the Chateaubriand, which we both thought was the best meal we had while there. The steak was really, really good, while the side dishes left a bit to be desired. We had really great service here, especially from the wine/water guy, so gave him a tip as well.Day 3: Taino. We had really bad service here. No waiter for at least 10 minutes, and we got our food before anyone offered us a drink. This was also an odd set-up. Payloads: a real ripoff. very bad value. room was dirty. hair in the bathtub and on the sink countertop. the bathmat had been left to rot in the bottom of the tub and was stained badly.room was poorly maintained. cracked plaster and paint in the main room with peeling wallpaper. the lamp between the beds had two light sockets with one socket broken apart with wires showing. mismatched tile repair in the shower, badly cracked ceiling in the bathroom with peeling paint. bed was lumpy and you could feel the springs underneath the thin layer of padding over them.for a $60/night, i might have tolerated some of these problems, but not at the $150/night that i was charged.restaurant was even a worse experience. on sunday, only offered a buffet. entree choices were beef in heavy gravy and grease soaked fried chicken with lots of untrimmed fat. by the time my wife got to the hot table, there was only fried chicken left. salad bar had a large bowl of lettuce with lots of old wilted lettuce left in the bowl. at $21/person, this buffet did not even include any drinks; soft drinks or otherwise. as we checked out of the hotel, we saw an advertising panel for a complete seafood buffet for $18.95/person. made me see red i was so angry. got no sympathy from the waiter either.i will never ever return to this hotel again under any circumstance and will recommend others avoid this same experience.stay here only if you absolutely must stay near the honolulu airport. even if this hotel were free, it would still be a bad value.

Payloads: excellent hotel i stayed here for business and was very happy with the quality of the hotel.check in was easy and the staff very welcoming. there is a starbucks in the lobby of the hotel which was great to pick up a coffee for the walk to the office in the morning.the rooms aren't large but the furnishings very modern and comfortable.i was supposed to stay 2 nights but my meetings were cancelled and therefore only stayed 1. there was no problem at all checking out early, and i was not charged a cancellation fee or the second night's rate, despite giving the hotel less than 24 hours notice, as their policy states. i was very impressed that the hotel did not try to 'double dip'.

Payloads: Loved Our Vacation My family and I just returned from a week-long stay at the Ocean Blue. We really had a wonderful time there and I don't understand the bad reviews that this resort has gotten. We stayed in Villa 6 within the resort. This villa was closest to the beach and yellow pool. This is the pool where all of the activities are held (water aerobics, poolside games, etc...) so it was a little nosier than the villas located by the blue pool. However, the noise was gone after the sun went down and the guests left the pool for dinner so this was not a problem. Our room was very spacious and always clean. We would leave a couple of dollars every day for our maid and she always left us a supply of water, towels and beer in our room. The rooms are dimly lit, as stated in many, many reviews. But I did not find this a problem. After spending a day in the sun, water and sand and then the evening with dinner and activities, we would go back to our room and sleep - you don't need bright lights for that.The service in the restaurants and bars are all pretty good. There were busy times when we didn't get our drinks or food immediately, but I never felt like I was ignored. The quality of the food was good as well. The buffets have a large variety of food. My one daughter is a very picky eater and she was always able to find something that she liked. The a la carte restaurants all have a different theme and we ate in all but 3 of them. The two that were our favorites were La Brasa and Margarita. Route 66 was probably our least favorite - the menu is pretty limited and the desserts aren't good at all. Mike's coffee house was wonderful - we went there at least once every day. They have a great selection of teas, hot and cold coffee drinks and snack items. The grounds were always clean. Payloads: love this hotel just returned from staying at the hyatt regency century plaza for a convention july 26-30th. pricey even at the convention rate but well worth the money. from the time i pulled into the valet parking area until i checked-out the hotel treated us as if we were the most important guests in the hotel. the hotel check-in was great our room wasn't ready but the lady at the desk put a hold on a room with 2 double beds and we were able to check in within the next hour. our bags were promptly brought to our room by a bell man. the room was wonderful with down duvet covers a table and two chairs (workstation), bedside chair and stand, mini-bar (which they emptied for a small fee so we could use the refrig.for our picnic supplies), closet with ironing board, safe, bathroom wonderful, and a coffee maker. we also had a nice view of the pool and mall next door. all rooms have sliding patio doors and a balcony. we felt like we were getting the star treatment. the hotel was able to handle a convention of over 1000 people and then turn around the day after and handle a high profile political person staying with them without compromising the convention activities. the hotel was located in a wonderful area 30 minutes from hollywood, 20-30 minutes from the grove, 10-15 minutes from beverly center, 30 minutes from lax. i would definately stay here again and recommend it to others.

Payloads: big let down we arrived at the hollywood roosevelt as a newley wed couple after a four and a half hour journey from the beautiful friendly ritz carlton hotel at lake las vegas. we walked into the hotel reception feeling like the beverly hillbillies, the staff at reception were cold and unfriendly although the receptionist did give us and upgrade to a cabana (which he said was overlooking the gardens! and was really overlooking a multistorey carpark with a vine growing up the side of it) the guy who took our bags to the room was friendly he gave us the ins and outs of the place. the hallways were dark, very dark, the cabana room was dark, not as chic as it looks on the website, even with the lights on you need a torch to see in your suitcase. the bathroom was about the same size as the wardrobe and the floor of the room wasnt very clean. all the furniture just looked cheap and tacky not great for the price! we ventured off for a drink (out of the hotel) and luckily we met a nice couple who was also staying in the roosevelt, after a few drinks we all decided to head back to the roosevelt and keep on drinking at the tropicana bar which is at the poolside at the roosevelt, i had this idea that it would be full of hollywood glamour and lots of beautiful people but it wasn't. everyone was dressed casually, very arrogant, rude and pretentious. the hotel was overrun with teenaged kids spending daddy's money. we were made to feel like intruders everytime we wanted to go to our room as the tropicana security staff would stop us and ask us where we were going and check us off their list, even if you had a bottle of water you were asked to get rid of it (but im just going to my room for gods sake!) don't even bother to ask any of the staff about the history of the hotel, because they don't know. just read it up before you go and educate them while your there. also don't bother saying hello or smiling at the staff because they just look at you like your off your trolley.the room was noisey all night long, the walls must be paper thin. loud music, car alarms, talking from the rooms nearby, dont even get me started on the airconditioning unit! honestly i thought this hotel was going to be chic, sexy elegent, classy, brimming with hollywood history and glamour and it was totally the opposite, which is a big shame. the owners of the hotel seriously need to reconsider who they are contracting the leases of the bars to as they are making this hotel a very uncomfortable place to stay. this hotel could be a magic piece of old hollywood if it was just managed properly. we left after two nights and i couldnt believe that while we were waiting for the car to be brought round for us to leave, the car valet guy told us which room marilyn monroe had lived in for two years and it was the room right across from ours. i'd asked the staff several times and no-one knew. i couldnt believe it i had walked past the room several times and the door had been open and i didnt get a proper look. :( over all a complete let down.

Payloads: we will stay at beverly garland's hotel again myself, my husband and my son stayed at beverly garland's holiday inn for 4 nights and enjoyed it very much. the room was a bit larger than most hotel rooms, and it was very clean. the pool was beautiful - we went swimming at night when the pool was lit up as well as the trees around the pool area (it was also heated which was perfect). i had no problems with the staff - they were very helpful. we enjoyed this hotel the best out of our trip to 3 cities in the states. as for location, it's not a beach hotel, but it only took 30 minutes to drive to santa monica beach from there. it's close to hollywood boulevard, and the shuttle to universal studios was good since we didn't have to pay for parking at the theme park ($15.00). the shuttle lets you off right at the entrance. also, if you buy your tickets to universal studios from the hotel, you can use them for two days instead of just one. there is noise from the 101 freeway, but i didn't notice because i was too tired from sightseeing all day. as for the hallways being dirty, i didn't find them horribly filthy - and besides, i wasn't sleeping in the hallway so it wasn't that much of a concern. to sum up, we will definitely be staying there again.
